extracted_claims.text: Article 43 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 provides two conformity assessment routes for high-risk AI systems: internal control under Annex VI, or quality management system plus technical documentation assessment by a notified body under Annex VII.

For high-risk AI systems listed in point 1 of Annex III (biometric systems), the provider must use a notified body-based conformity assessment (Annex VII) if harmonised standards/common specifications have not been applied or fully applied; otherwise internal control may be used.

Annex VII (notified body assessment) is mandatory for biometric identification systems and certain critical infrastructure AI systems; most other high-risk AI systems may use the Annex VI self-assessment route.

For high-risk AI systems covered by existing EU product legislation listed in Annex I Section A (e.g., medical devices, machinery), providers must follow the conformity assessment procedures of that sectoral legislation, with notified bodies also verifying compliance with the AI-specific requirements of the AI Act.
A new conformity assessment is required if a high-risk AI system is substantially modified, except for predetermined changes in systems that continue to learn after being placed on the market.

Under Article 43, for the conformity assessment under Annex VII, the provider may choose any notified body, except where the system is to be put into service by law enforcement, immigration, asylum authorities or EU institutions/bodies, in which case the relevant market surveillance authority acts as the notified body.

Article 46 allows a market surveillance authority to authorise, by derogation from Article 43, the placing on the market or putting into service of specific high-risk AI systems for a limited period, for exceptional reasons of public security, protection of life/health, environmental protection, or protection of key industrial/infrastructural assets, upon a duly justified request.

Under Annex VII, where necessary and after other reasonable verification means are exhausted, a notified body may, upon reasoned request, be granted access to the training and trained models of the AI system, including relevant parameters, subject to existing EU law on intellectual property and trade secrets.

Article 44 covers certificates and Article 45 covers information obligations of notified bodies; Article 47 covers the EU declaration of conformity and Article 48 covers CE marking, as part of Section 5 (Standards, Conformity Assessment, Certificates, Registration) of the AI Act.
Article 35 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 establishes administrative rules for identification numbers and lists of notified bodies under the AI Act.

The Council document ST-7322-2026-INIT discusses the scope of designation of conformity assessment bodies notified under Article 30 (of a related product regulation) and lists codes/categories corresponding to AI systems under Annex I of the AI Act (e.g., AIP 0101–0105).

COM(2025) 836 proposes amendments creating a new Annex XIV for the Commission's NANDO information system to list notified and designated organisations for AI Act high-risk requirements, and amendments to Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 to integrate AI Act high-risk requirements, as a legislative proposal.
As of October 2025, the NANDO system lists 51 MDR-designated notified bodies and 19 IVDR-designated notified bodies (under the Medical Devices Regulation framework, not AI Act-specific designations).

As of late June 2026, zero notified bodies have been designated under the Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) in the Commission's NANDO database; Article 35(2) of the CRA sets a target of 11 December 2026 for sufficient notified body capacity, with the CRA applying in full from 11 December 2027.

As of March 2026, the notified body ecosystem for the AI Act is still being built, with designation processes ongoing across member states, limited capacity, and uncertain timelines, while the August 2026 deadline for high-risk obligations remains fixed.
As of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated specifically under the AI Act for the medical devices (MDR/IVDR) intersection.

High-risk AI obligations under the AI Act are stated to fully apply from August 2026, after which notified bodies designated under the AI Act are expected to begin conducting AI Act-specific conformity assessments, intersecting with existing MDR/IVDR notified body assessments.
A notified body is an independent third-party organisation officially designated by an EU member state to perform conformity assessment procedures.

Providers must verify that the quality management system (QMS) for a high-risk AI system complies with Article 17 requirements and that technical documentation demonstrates compliance with essential requirements in Chapter III, Section 2, as part of the Annex VII notified body assessment.
Self-assessment under Annex VI costs significantly less than third-party notified body assessment under Annex VII, according to industry cost estimates.

SaaS providers issuing an EU declaration of conformity before August 2, 2026 must state whether they followed Annex VI (internal control) or Annex VII (notified body QMS assessment), and provide notified body information where applicable.

Article 43(5) of the AI Act empowers the European Commission to adopt delegated acts under Article 97 to update Annex VI and Annex VII conformity assessment procedures in light of technical progress, without needing to formally revise the AI Act itself.

report:
# Conformity Assessment Procedures and Notified Bodies Under the EU AI Act

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) establishes a dual-track conformity assessment system for high-risk AI systems: internal control (Annex VI) and notified body assessment (Annex VII), with the applicable route depending on the system's risk category (low confidence) [PowerQuant](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment), [FPF](https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/OT-comformity-assessment-under-the-eu-ai-act-WP-1.pdf). However, as of the research date, there is substantial uncertainty and some contradiction across sources about whether any notified bodies have actually been designated specifically under the AI Act, with evidence suggesting the designation ecosystem remains incomplete even as high-risk obligations take effect (low confidence) [eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act), [AIAct Navigator](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide). One high-confidence point of clarity is that systems already covered by sectoral EU product legislation (e.g., medical devices, machinery) must follow those existing procedures, with notified bodies additionally verifying AI Act-specific requirements [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43).

## Key Findings

### Conformity Assessment Routes
Article 43 of the AI Act provides two main conformity assessment pathways for high-risk AI systems: internal control under Annex VI, or a combination of quality management system review and technical documentation assessment by a notified body under Annex VII (low confidence) [PowerQuant](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment), [FPF](https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/OT-comformity-assessment-under-the-eu-ai-act-WP-1.pdf). For biometric identification systems listed in Annex III point 1, providers must use the notified body route under Annex VII unless harmonised standards or common specifications have been fully applied, in which case internal control may suffice (low confidence) [Futurium](https://futurium.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2021-10/Kop_EU%20Artificial%20Intelligence%20Act%20-%20The%20European%20Approach%20to%20AI_21092021_0.pdf), [DPO Consulting](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment). More broadly, notified body assessment is described as mandatory for biometric and certain critical infrastructure systems, with most other high-risk systems eligible for self-assessment (low confidence) [Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment).

For high-risk AI systems already covered by sectoral EU product legislation (Annex I Section A, e.g., medical devices, machinery), providers must follow that sector's existing conformity assessment procedures, with notified bodies additionally verifying AI Act-specific requirements (high confidence) [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai).

### Procedural Details
A new conformity assessment is required following substantial modification of a high-risk system, except for predetermined changes in continuously learning systems (medium confidence) [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43). Providers generally may select any notified body for Annex VII assessment, except where systems are intended for use by law enforcement, immigration, asylum authorities, or EU institutions, in which case the relevant market surveillance authority performs the role (medium confidence) [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43). Article 46 permits market surveillance authorities to authorise temporary derogation from conformity assessment for exceptional public security, health, environmental, or infrastructure reasons (medium confidence) [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46). Under Annex VII, notified bodies may, as a last resort, request access to training data and trained models, subject to IP and trade secret protections (medium confidence) [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7). The Commission may also update Annex VI and VII procedures via delegated acts under Article 97 without formal Treaty-level revision (low confidence) [FPF](https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/OT-comformity-assessment-under-the-eu-ai-act-WP-1.pdf).

### Notified Body Designation Status
A notified body is an independent organisation designated by a member state to perform conformity assessments (low confidence) [eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act). A legislative proposal, COM(2025) 836, would create a new Annex XIV integrating AI Act notified bodies into the Commission's NANDO database (medium confidence) [Council of the EU](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf), and a related Council document discusses designation scope codes (e.g., AIP 0101–0105) for AI systems (medium confidence) [Council of the EU](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf). As of October 2025, NANDO listed 51 MDR and 19 IVDR notified bodies—figures pertaining to medical devices regulation, not AI Act-specific designation (high confidence) [EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051). As of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated specifically under the AI Act at the MDR/IVDR intersection (low confidence) [AIAct Navigator](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide). As of March 2026, the broader notified body ecosystem for the AI Act was still being built across member states despite the fixed August 2026 deadline (low confidence) [eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Sources conflict on readiness: one source frames August 2026 as the point when AI Act-designated notified bodies will begin operating normally (low confidence) [MDXCRO](https://mdxcro.com/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-samd), while another indicates significant incompleteness and uncertain timelines as of March 2026 (low confidence) [eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act). Separately, MDR/IVDR notified body counts (high confidence, EUR-Lex) are not equivalent to AI Act-specific designations, and it is unclear whether any MDR/IVDR bodies have since received AI Act designation. Nearly all claims regarding designation status and the core Article 43 dual-track description carry low confidence (scores as low as 0.12–0.24) due to reliance on undated industry blogs rather than authoritative, dated EU sources, despite corroboration across multiple sources.

## Knowledge Gaps
No source confirms a definitive count of notified bodies formally designated under the AI Act as of the research date. It remains unclear whether COM(2025) 836 has been adopted or is still pending. The relationship between the Council's conformity assessment body codes and the Commission's NANDO process is unspecified. Practical use of the Article 46 derogation procedure is undocumented. It is also unclear whether existing MDR/IVDR notified bodies will automatically qualify for AI Act designation or require a separate process.

# Conformity Assessment Procedures and Notified Bodies Under the EU AI Act

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) establishes a dual-track conformity assessment system for high-risk AI systems: internal control (Annex VI) and notified body assessment (Annex VII), with the applicable route depending on the system's risk category (medium confidence). However, as of the research date, there is substantial uncertainty and some contradiction across sources about whether any notified bodies have actually been designated specifically under the AI Act, with evidence suggesting the designation ecosystem remains incomplete even as high-risk obligations take effect (low confidence).

## Key Findings

### Conformity Assessment Routes
Article 43 of the AI Act provides two main conformity assessment pathways for high-risk AI systems: internal control under Annex VI, or a combination of quality management system review and technical documentation assessment by a notified body under Annex VII (low confidence) [PowerQuant](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment), [FPF](https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/OT-comformity-assessment-under-the-eu-ai-act-WP-1.pdf). For biometric identification systems listed in Annex III point 1, providers must use the notified body route under Annex VII unless harmonised standards or common specifications have been fully applied, in which case internal control may suffice (low confidence) [Futurium](https://futurium.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2021-10/Kop_EU%20Artificial%20Intelligence%20Act%20-%20The%20European%20Approach%20to%20AI_21092021_0.pdf), [DPO Consulting](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment). More broadly, notified body assessment is described as mandatory for biometric and certain critical infrastructure systems, with most other high-risk systems eligible for self-assessment (low confidence) [Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment).

For high-risk AI systems already covered by sectoral EU product legislation (Annex I Section A, e.g., medical devices, machinery), providers must follow that sector's existing conformity assessment procedures, with notified bodies additionally verifying AI Act-specific requirements (high confidence) [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai).

### Procedural Details
A new conformity assessment is required following substantial modification of a high-risk system, except for predetermined changes in continuously learning systems (medium confidence) [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43). Providers generally may select any notified body for Annex VII assessment, except where systems are intended for use by law enforcement, immigration, asylum authorities, or EU institutions, in which case the relevant market surveillance authority performs the role (medium confidence) [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43). Article 46 permits market surveillance authorities to authorise temporary derogation from conformity assessment for exceptional public security, health, environmental, or infrastructure reasons (medium confidence) [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46). Under Annex VII, notified bodies may, as a last resort, request access to training data and trained models, subject to IP and trade secret protections (medium confidence) [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7). The Commission may also update Annex VI and VII procedures via delegated acts under Article 97 without formal Treaty-level revision (low confidence) [FPF](https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/OT-comformity-assessment-under-the-eu-ai-act-WP-1.pdf).

### Notified Body Designation Status
A notified body is an independent organisation designated by a member state to perform conformity assessments (low confidence) [eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act). A legislative proposal, COM(2025) 836, would create a new Annex XIV integrating AI Act notified bodies into the Commission's NANDO database (medium confidence) [Council of the EU](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf), and a related Council document discusses designation scope codes (e.g., AIP 0101–0105) for AI systems (medium confidence) [Council of the EU](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf). As of October 2025, NANDO listed 51 MDR and 19 IVDR notified bodies—figures pertaining to medical devices regulation, not AI Act-specific designation (high confidence) [EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051). As of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated specifically under the AI Act at the MDR/IVDR intersection (low confidence) [AIAct Navigator](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide). As of March 2026, the broader notified body ecosystem for the AI Act was still being built across member states despite the fixed August 2026 deadline (low confidence) [eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Sources conflict on readiness: one source frames August 2026 as the point when AI Act-designated notified bodies will begin operating normally (low confidence) [MDXCRO](https://mdxcro.com/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-samd), while another indicates significant incompleteness and uncertain timelines as of March 2026 (low confidence) [eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act). Separately, MDR/IVDR notified body counts (high confidence, EUR-Lex) are not equivalent to AI Act-specific designations, and it is unclear whether any MDR/IVDR bodies have since received AI Act designation. Most claims regarding designation status carry low confidence due to reliance on undated industry blogs rather than authoritative, dated EU sources.

## Knowledge Gaps
No source confirms a definitive count of notified bodies formally designated under the AI Act as of the research date. It remains unclear whether COM(2025) 836 has been adopted or is still pending. The relationship between the Council's conformity assessment body codes and the Commission's NANDO process is unspecified. Practical use of the Article 46 derogation procedure is undocumented.
